base.description: Chassis with the common equipment seated: both supervisors and system controllers, three fan trays, six fabric modules, five 3 kW AC supplies with a blank over each of the other five slots, and sixteen line-card blanks.
base.source: derived - Cisco publishes no bundle for the Nexus 9516 in the guide, so the library defines one from the guide's own power-budget example (Planning for Power Requirements, Step 1, PDF p20, printed 14: two supervisor A, two N9K-SC-A system controllers, sixteen line cards, six fabric modules at 504 W, the N9K-C9516-FM's maximum, and three fan trays, 13,227 W in all): those parts in their slots, six N9K-C9516-FM in FM 1 to FM 6, three N9K-C9516-FAN, and a line-card blank in each of the sixteen line-card slots. Step 2 of the example says the load needs five supplies (13,224 W over 3,000 W is 4.41, rounded up to five; the same sentence also says "rounded up to three", a slip), and the supply type is the library's choice: five N9K-PAC-3000W-B in PS 1 to PS 5 (grid A), with a blank over each other supply slot. The example names no supply and no line-card blank.

empty.description: The chassis with every supervisor, system-controller, fan-tray and fabric-module bay empty, a blank over each power-supply slot and a line-card blank in each line-card slot. An illustration of what the bays look like with nothing seated.

fabric-e.description: Five N9K-C9516-FM-E fabric modules in FM 2 to FM 6 (the guide says five FM-E must be in those slots) and the N9K-C9516-FM-CV blank in FM 1. An illustration: the guide prints no ordering code for it.

fabric-three.description: Three N9K-C9516-FM-E2 fabric modules in FM 2, FM 4 and FM 6, as the guide's slot rule puts three, and the N9K-C9516-FM-CV blank in each odd slot. An illustration: the guide prints no ordering code for it.

psu-dc.description: The base with five N9K-PDC-3000W-B -48 V DC supplies in PS 1 to PS 5. An illustration: the guide prints no ordering code for a build with this supply.

psu-dual-input.description: The base with five N9K-PUV2-3000W-B dual-input universal AC/DC supplies in PS 1 to PS 5. An illustration: the guide prints no ordering code for a build with this supply.

psu-universal.description: The base with five N9K-PUV-3000W-B universal AC/DC supplies in PS 1 to PS 5. An illustration: the guide prints no ordering code for a build with this supply.

description: Cisco Nexus 9516 - the 21 RU, sixteen-line-card modular chassis of the Nexus 9500 family, running NX-OS mode. The FRONT carries the chassis lamps across the top, sixteen line-card slots LC 1 to LC 16 from top to bottom, two supervisor slots SUP 1 and SUP 2 side by side below them, and ten power-supply slots PS 1 to PS 10 standing on end along the bottom. The REAR carries three fan trays FAN 1 to FAN 3, six fabric-module slots FM 1 to FM 6 behind the fan trays, and two system controllers SC 1 and SC 2 below them. Air enters at the front and leaves at the rear. Each line-card slot holds its blank and accepts the line-card blank and three of the four line cards modelled so far (N9K-X9736C-FX, N9K-X97160YC-EX and N9K-X9732C-FX; the N9K-X9716D-GX is not compatible with this switch); the other 9500 line cards follow.

gaps.note: The guide gives a typical and maximum draw per module and no figure for the chassis itself; the chassis total is whatever its occupants sum to. Each line card carries its own typical and maximum draw, so a loaded chassis's total is the sum of its occupants; none is written here.
gaps.wanted: a chassis-level draw from Cisco, or confirmation that the sum of the module table is the answer

gaps.note: Which fabric module each line card goes with, and how many are needed, is listed here and NOT ENFORCED: no bay or card restricts the fabric module it is seated with. The guide's Overview Table 1 (PDF pp7-8, printed 1-2) pairs the cards modelled here with the N9K-C9516-FM-E and -FM-E2 (this chassis has no -G fabric module); the count is the fabric modules required for maximum bandwidth, read by line order. N9K-X9736C-FX: FM-E 5, FM-E2 5. N9K-X97160YC-EX: FM-E 4, FM-E2 4. N9K-X9732C-FX: FM-E 4, FM-E2 4 plus 1 redundant. The N9K-X9716D-GX appears in no row: it is not compatible with this switch. The guide's notes: FM 5 (slot 25) works only with the N9K-X9736C-FX, N9K-X9736Q-FX and N9K-X9736C-FX3 (PDF p9, printed 3); a N9516 "having 16 x N9K-X9788TC-FX line cards require a minimum of 3 FM-E2" (the note under the FM-E row, PDF p8, printed 2; that card is not modelled); and "Do not mix ACI-mode line cards with NX-OS mode line cards in the same switch" (PDF p7, printed 1). Its "Migrate the switch to 400-Gigabit -GX line cards" (PDF p113, printed 107) copies the 9508 guide's sentences about N9K-C9508-FM-G modules, for a card the same guide says this switch does not take.
gaps.wanted: a restriction in the format between a card and the fabric modules it is seated with

gaps.note: The 9516's own planning table (PDF p19, printed 13) gives the supervisors 80 W maximum for the N9K-SUP-A, N9K-SUP-A+ and N9K-SUP-B+ and 90 W for the N9K-SUP-B, and the worked example counts 2 x 80 W. The shared supervisor parts carry 90 W maximum (from the 9508 and 9504 tables) and are not edited here. The 9516's seated supervisors therefore read 10 W high each in a power total, except the N9K-SUP-B.
gaps.wanted: a corrected version of the shared supervisors, in its own pull request, or Cisco's single figure

gaps.note: The clearance figure (PDF p25, printed 19, with its callout row on the same page) gives the width of the chassis plus the vertical mounting brackets as 19.2 in (48.8 cm). The ear model has no field for an overall width, so the mounting-bracket region is not sized by it and the front face stays the 444.5 mm chassis width.
gaps.wanted: ear support for an overall width, or a dimensioned front view of the bracket

gaps.note: The guide's rack kit is N9K-C9500-RMK (PDF p31, printed 25; contents in Table 5, PDF p135, printed 129), with the accessory kit N9K-ACC-KIT (printed N9K-C9500-ACK in Appendix C). The library has a kit contract for the N9K-C9500-RMK, but listing it here would break lint while it says `unplaced:`, and removing the sentence edits a shared part. No kit is listed.
gaps.wanted: a follow-up that drops the sentence from the shared kit and lists the kits on the 9508, 9504 and 9516

gaps.note: The guide's DC supply procedures say "Verify that the Input 1 (IN1) and Input 2 (IN2) LEDs light up on the power supply" (PDF p45, printed 39, and p112, printed 106), but its Power Supply LEDs table lists only OK and FAIL (PDF p133, printed 127), and the shared N9K-PDC-3000W-B draws OK and FAIL only. The IN1 and IN2 lamps are not drawn, and the supply is not edited here.
gaps.wanted: the position and colours of the DC supply's IN1 and IN2 lamps, drawn in a new version of the supply

gaps.note: The guide says a blank module sits in an empty supervisor or system-controller slot ("remove the blank module that is already in that slot. Unscrew its captive screw", PDF p79, printed 73, and p82, printed 76) and gives it no part number, drawing or dimension. The supervisor and system-controller bays therefore show nothing when empty.
gaps.wanted: the part number and a drawing of the supervisor and system-controller slot blanks

gaps.note: The guide has no flat front or rear elevation, and the NetBox elevations are not held. Every position on both faces is derived from the dimension table and the arrangement in the isometric figures; see the front-stack and rear-stack provenance. No position is measured.
gaps.wanted: a flat front and rear elevation of the chassis with dimensions, or the NetBox elevation images

gaps.note: The bay sizes are the module envelopes of the dimension table, and the positions are the stack derived from them; none is a measurement of the chassis. The fan-tray bays and the fabric-module bays occupy the same area of the rear face because the fabric modules are behind the fan trays.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned rear view with the fan trays removed

gaps.note: The side and top faces are named in the figures (handles on both sides, mounting bracket, rack rail positions) and no figure dimensions any feature on them, so those faces carry regions with no coordinates. The bottom face is empty: no view of it is published.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned side and top view

attrs.redundancy-note: n+1 - hardware guide, "Overview" Table 1 "Supported Fabric Modules and Line Cards": the number of fabric modules required for maximum bandwidth is three to five by line card, and the N9K-C9516-FM-E2 with the N9K-X9736C-FX3 and similar cards takes "4 (+1 redundant)". Three to six fabric modules are supported, in the slots the Overview note names.

2+1 - hardware guide, "Replacing a Fan Tray" (PDF p89, printed 83): "The switch uses three fan trays. It can operate with two fan trays while you replace one"; the other trays speed up their fans when one is removed.
n+1 - hardware guide, "Overview of Power Modes": combined, n+1 and n+n modes; n+1 needs at least one supply more than the number the modules need, n+n twice that, half on each source.

1+1 - hardware guide, "Overview of Supervisor Modules": one or two supervisors; with two, one is active and the other standby, and the standby takes over if the active goes down. Both must be the same type.
1+1 - hardware guide, "Installing or Replacing a System Controller Module": the switch can operate with one or two system controllers; one is replaced while the other is installed.

name: n9k-c9516

airflow.note: datasheet - "Air intake from the cold aisle for all modules and power supplies" and "Air exhaust to the hot aisle" (clearance figure, PDF p25, printed 19, callouts 4 and 5), and "port-side intake airflow" for every supply. The chassis is front-to-back.

chassis.note: datasheet - Appendix A "Switch Dimensions" (PDF p115, printed 109): "Cisco N9516 chassis: width 17.5 inches (44.5 cm); depth 31.76 inches (80.67 cm) for chassis and handles; height 36.70 inches (93.41 cm) (21 RU)". Modelled as 444.5 x 933.45 x 806.7 mm. CONFLICT ON HEIGHT: 36.70 in is 932.2 mm, the same cell's 93.41 cm is 934.1 mm, the rack text and rail steps say "21-RU (36.7 inches or 93.4 cm)" (PDF p24, printed 18; PDF pp32-35, printed 26-29), and 21 x 44.45 mm is 933.45 mm; the cell's own RU count, 933.45 mm, is used, which is also what the front stack of modules adds up to. CONFLICT ON DEPTH: the clearance figure (PDF p25, printed 19, callout 11) gives the chassis depth as 33.15 in (84.2 cm), the same drawing as the 9504's; the table's 31.76 in (80.67 cm) is used because it is the stated dimension "for chassis and handles", and the figure's number is not explained. Chassis weight 192.0 lb (87.3 kg), PDF p116 (printed 110).

chassis-lamps-position.note: estimated - Appendix B "Chassis LEDs" (PDF p129, printed 123) says the lamps are "located at the top of the front of the chassis", which this figure agrees with. The legends BCN, SUP, FAB, IOM, PSU, FAN and PWR MGMT are plain text as the guide prints them; the vendor logo is not drawn, and a logo-zone is reserved.

ears-and-kits.note: drawing - the clearance figure (PDF p25, printed 19) shows the chassis between front and rear vertical rack posts with its front at the front posts, and the front figure (PDF p10, printed 4, callout 4) shows "2 vertical mounting brackets used to mount the chassis onto a rack" at the sides of the front. The rack-mount figure (PDF p38, printed 32) shows the chassis mounting brackets against the rack's vertical rails. The shipped position is therefore flush, and no `at` is written: no figure gives the bracket's depth position. The clearance figure (PDF p25, printed 19, and its callout row, same page) prints "Width of the chassis plus vertical mounting brackets on each side" as 19.2 in (48.8 cm), against the 17.5 in chassis: about 21.6 mm of bracket on each side. The ear model takes a depth offset and a height and no width, so that span is carried here and in a gap, not drawn. A rear-mount position is not given by the guide. The shipment list (PDF p31, printed 25) names "Rack mount kit for the Cisco N9516 (N9K-C9500-RMK) chassis" and the "Switch accessory kit (N9K-ACC-KIT)"; Appendix C Table 5 (PDF p135, printed 129) lists the N9K-C9500-RMK contents and prints the accessory kit as N9K-C9500-ACK. The bottom-support rails carry the weight; the rack must be a four-post rack 24 to 32 in (61.0 to 81.3 cm) deep between its front and rear rails (PDF p24, printed 18; the rails' span again on PDF p32, printed 26). No kit is listed under `chassis.kits`: a listed kit that still says `unplaced:` fails lint, and removing the sentence edits a shared kit, so the kits are a follow-up pull request.

environmental.note: datasheet - Appendix A "Environmental Specifications" (PDF p115, printed 109), transcribed. CONFLICT ON ALTITUDE: the "Altitude Requirements" paragraph (PDF p14, printed 8) says 10,000 ft (3048 m), and 6,562 ft (2000 m) for China; the Appendix A table says 0 to 13,123 ft (0 to 4,000 m). The table is used, and the paragraph is recorded here.

fabric-slots.note: datasheet - "Overview" slot rules and notes (PDF p9, printed 3): three fabric modules go in FM 2, 4 and 6; four in FM 2, 3, 4 and 6; five in FM 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 or alternatively FM 2 to 6; five FM-E or FM-E2 in FM 2 to 6; six in FM 1 to 6. Fabric slots FM 2, FM 4 and FM 6 must be filled with functioning fabric modules or with blank modules with power connectors (N9K-C9516-FM-Z), which provide power to the fan trays covering those modules, and an empty FM 1, FM 3 or FM 5 takes the blank N9K-C9516-FM-CV. An empty odd slot defaults to the FM-CV, an empty even slot to the FM-Z. The fan-tray lamp table (PDF p131, printed 125) lists the FM and FM-E as powering the tray and leaves out the FM-E2: the omission is recorded and the FM-E2 is accepted in every slot. A bay holds any module or blank; the pairing rules are the guide's and are not enforced by the model. The migration caution (PDF p114, printed 108) names "N9K-C950x-FM-G-Z", the 9508 guide's text copied; no part is made from it.

front-stack.note: estimated - every position on the front is derived, not measured. The guide's front figure (PDF p10, printed 4) is an isometric drawing, so no aspect check (Gate 1) can be made. The layout follows that figure's arrangement and the guide's dimension table: a top band for the chassis lamps (callout 5); sixteen line cards of 1.75 in (44.45 mm) stacked top to bottom; the two supervisors, 1.75 in high and 8.0 in (203.2 mm) wide with brackets, side by side; and ten power supplies standing on end, 5.25 in (133.35 mm) tall and 1.75 in (44.45 mm) wide, in a row at the bottom. The arithmetic closes: 44.45 + 16 x 44.45 + 44.45 + 133.35 = 933.45 mm, and ten supplies of 44.45 mm span 444.5 mm, the chassis width. The cage is taken as the 17.0 in (431.8 mm) line-card width, centred in the 444.5 mm face. The figure shows nine supplies and a plain blank in the fourth slot; that is one photograph of one build and is not carried. The seven chassis lamps are read from the figure's strip at the top, which sits left of centre and is about a quarter of the face wide: they are put at an even pitch across it.

lifecycle.note: datasheet - Cisco has announced the end of sale of the Nexus 9516 chassis: "End-of-Sale and End-of-Life Announcement for the Cisco N9500 Cloud-scale 16-slot Chassis and Components", https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/products/collateral/switches/nexus-9000-series-switches/n9500-cloud-16-slot-chassis-comp-eol.html (the title names a group of parts and no date is held, so none is written). Sale status of each module is per module: N9K-C9516-FM is end-of-sale by its own notice; the others have no status and are recorded as unknown.

line-cards.note: datasheet - the sixteen line-card slots accept the line-card blank N9K-C9500-LC-CV and the line cards this guide supports among those modelled: N9K-X9736C-FX, N9K-X97160YC-EX and N9K-X9732C-FX, which Overview Table 1 and the power tables (PDF pp7-8 and 18-20, printed 1-2 and 12-14) list. A line card is accepted because this chassis's own guide supports it. The N9K-X9716D-GX is NOT accepted: the Overview says "The N9K-X9716D-GX line card is not compatible with this switch" (PDF p7, printed 1), and that sentence wins over the Planning for Power table (PDF p18, printed 12), which is a copy of the 9508's, names the 9508's fabric modules and still lists the card. The other 9500 line cards follow in later batches; the N9K-X9788TC-FX is listed in the guide and not modelled, because the guides name its 48 ports three ways and no figure of its faceplate is held.

power-slots.note: datasheet - "Overview of Power Modes" (PDF pp70-73, printed 64-67): with grid redundancy PS 1 to PS 5 go to one source (grid A) and PS 6 to PS 10 to the other (grid B), PDF p71 (printed 65) and p73 (printed 67); "up to five with the combined power mode, up to six with n+1, or up to ten with n+n" (PDF p9, printed 3). The guide contradicts itself on mixing supply types: "The switch can be powered by a mix of AC, DC, HVAC/HVDC power sources" (PDF p10, printed 4, and p23, printed 17) against "Do not use a mix of AC and DC power sources for a switch" (PDF p118, printed 112). Every supply type is accepted by every slot.

power-tables.note: datasheet - "Planning for Power Requirements" holds two tables. The first (PDF pp17-19, printed 11-13) is a copy of the 9508's, naming N9K-C9508-* parts; the chassis's own table (PDF pp19-20, printed 13-14) is used for every module here, and the copy is recorded as a conflict. The own table's FM-E and FM-E2 share one row printed on two lines (980 W / 1320 W and 439 W / 900 W, typical and maximum) and are read BY LINE ORDER, FM-E first; no worked example confirms either. The worked example (PDF p20, printed 14) counts two supervisor A at 80 W, two system controllers at 25 W, sixteen line cards at 540 W, six fabric modules at 504 W, which confirms the FM row, and three fan trays at "3 x 451 W = 1353 W", which matches neither fan figure in the table (330 W typical, 600 W maximum): total 13,227 W. Step 2 says that 13,224 W over 3,000 W needs "five power supplies" and in the same sentence "rounded up to three": a slip, and the arithmetic (4.41, rounded up) gives five.

rear-stack.note: estimated - the rear is derived the same way. The guide's rear figure (PDF p11, printed 5) is isometric. Three fan trays of 5.04 in (128.02 mm) are centred across the width, each 32.08 in (814.83 mm) tall with its brackets; the six fabric modules, 2.46 in (62.48 mm) wide and 30.4 in (772.16 mm) tall, sit behind them on a pitch of half a fan tray, so FM 1 and FM 2 are behind FAN 1, FM 3 and FM 4 behind FAN 2, FM 5 and FM 6 behind FAN 3 (the guide says the even-numbered fabric slot is the one behind a fan tray that powers it, PDF p131, printed 125). The two system controllers, 7.81 in (198.37 mm) wide with brackets and 1.42 in (36.07 mm) high, sit below the fan trays. The margin above the fan trays is estimated. In the rear figure (fig-0013, PDF p11) the controllers sit in a recessed tray that runs the full width of the face under the fan trays; it is drawn as a full-width panel from the fan trays' lower end (821.18 mm) to the foot of the face, and the controllers stand near its top, about 18 mm below its edge and inset 23.85 mm from each side, estimated by laying the figure's tray, fan-tray foot and controller edges against the face height (the figure is isometric, so this is a ratio, not a measurement). The fan trays keep the guide's 32.08 in height: the figure's fan-tray foot, read the same way, falls at about 808 mm, within the isometric error of that figure.

ru.note: datasheet - 21 RU, printed in the dimensions table (PDF p115, printed 109) and in "Rack and Cabinet Requirements" (PDF p24, printed 18). "Fully loaded, the switch weighs up to 568 lb (258 kg)" (PDF p35, printed 29) is carried as an attribute, not as the chassis weight.

slots.note: datasheet - "Overview" (PDF p7, printed 1, and p9, printed 3): supervisor modules in slots SUP 1 and SUP 2 (modules 27 and 28), system controllers in SC 1 and SC 2 (modules 29 and 30), line cards in LC 1 to LC 16 (top to bottom; the guide's "Modules 1 and 16" is a slip for 1 to 16), fabric modules in FM 1 to FM 6 (slots 21 to 26, left to right), fan trays in FAN 1 to FAN 3 (modules 41 to 43) and power supplies in PS 1 to PS 10 (modules 31 to 40, left to right). "Slots are numbered from left to right or from top to bottom" (PDF p10, printed 4). Numbering is the guide's; whether each label is printed on the metal is not shown by any figure the guide gives.

sources.note: Cisco N9516 NX-OS Mode Switch Hardware Installation Guide (138 pp; first published 2014-06-24, last modified 2026-09-17), https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/td/docs/switches/datacenter/nexus9000/hw/n9516_hig/guide/b_n9516_hardware_installation_guide.pdf (page numbers below are PDF pages with the printed page after them, six lower: "PDF p10 (printed 4)"). Cisco's Nexus 9508 and 9504 hardware installation guides were read to confirm the parts the three chassis share; each chassis cites its own guide. The NetBox devicetype-library has no 9516 device type, and the module-type files it lists for the 9516 and its images were NOT available to this work - only a path listing of that library is - so no NetBox elevation was compared. No data sheet, photograph, 3D model or stencil is held for the 9516. The guide has no flat front or rear view and prints no figure caption: both faces were read from its isometric figures on PDF p10 (printed 4) and p11 (printed 5).
